# Design

Within [environment engineering](../README.md), design turns the author's [identified intent](../intent.md) into a causal hypothesis and an intervention in documentation, code, or both. It uses [theory](../theory.md) to explain why changing an environmental cause should produce the desirable effects and avoid the important undesirable effects for the applicable `participant`, `situation`, and `encounter-noise` inputs.

Design applies to the affected `total-environment` established with intent, including its relevant state and cross-boundary dependencies. An intervention may edit one surface, but its hypothesis must trace the material causes on which its effects depend across that complete boundary.

Humans and agents encounter one `total-environment`. Design therefore applies two distinct methods to the same proposed intervention rather than creating a human environment and an agent environment. Each method follows its participant's cognitive mechanism, but both must preserve one meaning, authority structure, action model, and state model.

The resulting designs must be compatible and co-beneficial. A cue, affordance, constraint, response, or state introduced for one participant class cannot contradict or quietly obstruct the other. Across the complete result, the chosen causes must also reinforce both participant classes rather than merely avoid conflict. Clear terminology can support human schemas and agent context conditioning; visible state and precise feedback can support human recovery and agent continuation; executable constraints can protect both.

Apply each method for every applicable participant. Not every individual cause must benefit both participant classes. When an intervention needs participant-specific expression, keep the shared semantics canonical and make the complete result reinforce rather than duplicate or replace them. A benefit for one participant does not compensate for an important undesirable effect on another.

## Human

[Human design](human.md) shapes schema activation, conceptual execution, action, feedback, and recovery for human participants in their actual situations.

## Agent

[Agent design](agent.md) shapes context conditioning, instruction interpretation, tool use, state recovery, and verification for agent participants in their actual harnesses.
